'''Armed conflicts and attacks'''
*[[Russian invasion of Ukraine]]
**[[Attacks in Russia during the Russian invasion of Ukraine]]
***[[Ukraine]] launches [[drone warfare|drone attacks]] on multiple [[Oblasts of Russia]], including [[Moscow]], prompting all flights to be suspended at [[Vnukovo International Airport]] and [[Moscow Domodedovo Airport]]. [[Governor of Bryansk Oblast|Bryansk Governor]] [[Alexander Bogomaz]] says that at least 59 Ukrainian [[Unmanned combat aerial vehicle|drones]] have been shot down over the region. Russia also reports that two people were killed in the Ukrainian drone attack on Moscow. [https://www.reuters.com/world/europe/russia-destroys-ukraine-launched-drone-flying-towards-moscow-mayor-says-2024-09-09/ (Reuters)] [https://www.timesofisrael.com/liveblog_entry/child-killed-in-ukrainian-drone-attack-on-moscow-russia-says/ (''Times of Israel'')]
**[[Iran and the Russian invasion of Ukraine]], [[International sanctions against Iran]]
***[[United States Secretary of State|U.S. Secretary of State]] [[Antony Blinken]] says that [[Russia]] has received a shipment of [[Fath 360]] [[tactical ballistic missile]]s from [[Iran]], and expects their deployment "within weeks". Iran denies the claim, calling it "[[psychological warfare]]". In response, the [[United Kingdom]], [[France]], and [[Germany]] announce new sanctions on Iran for supplying Russia with ballistic missiles. [https://www.bbc.com/news/articles/c75n2wnkp1vo (BBC News)] [https://www.telegraph.co.uk/world-news/2024/09/10/israel-hamas-war-latest-news-airstrikes-mawasi-gaza/ (''The Telegraph'')]
**[[List of military aid to Ukraine during the Russo-Ukrainian War|Military aid to Ukraine during the Russo-Ukrainian War]]
***The [[Netherlands]] lifts all of its weapons restrictions on [[military equipment]] that it provided to Ukraine, allowing the [[Armed Forces of Ukraine|Ukrainian military]] to target Russia with long-range weapons, while also urging [[NATO]] allies to lift their own weapons restrictions. [https://www.kyivpost.com/post/38760 (Kyiv Post)] 
*[[Gaza war]]
**[[Israeli invasion of the Gaza Strip]]
***At least 40 people are killed and more than 60 others are injured in an [[Israel]]i [[airstrike]] on the [[Al-Mawasi, Rafah|Al-Mawasi]] [[refugee camp]] in [[Rafah]] in the [[Gaza Strip]]. Twenty tents housing [[internally displaced person|displaced people]] are destroyed during the attack. [https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2024/9/10/heinous-at-least-40-killed-in-israeli-attack-on-tent-camp-officials-say (Al Jazeera)]
***The [[Israel Defense Forces|Israeli military]] says the strike targeted senior [[Hamas]] commanders operating in a command center embedded inside a designated [[humanitarian corridor|humanitarian area]] whom the Israel Defense Forces says were all involved in the [[October 7 attacks]]. [https://english.alarabiya.net/News/middle-east/2024/09/10/israeli-military-says-it-struck-senior-hamas-commanders-in-gaza (Al Arabiya)] [https://www.timesofisrael.com/dozens-said-killed-as-idf-targets-prominent-hamas-operatives-in-gaza-tent-camp/ (''Times of Israel'')]
*[[Israel–Hezbollah conflict (2023–present)|Israel–Hezbollah conflict]]
**A [[Redwan Force]] commander is killed and fourteen [[civilian]]s are injured in Israeli airstrikes on [[Saghbine]] and [[Rachaf]] in [[southern Lebanon|southern]] [[Lebanon]]. [https://www.aljazeera.com/news/liveblog/2024/9/10/israels-war-on-gaza-live-israel-held-polio-vaccinators-at-gun-point-un  (Al Jazeera)]

'''Disasters and accidents'''
*The death toll from the [[capsizing]] of a migrant boat off the coast of [[Senegal]] over the weekend increases to 26 after the discovery of 17 more bodies. [https://www.reuters.com/world/africa/death-toll-capsized-migrant-boat-offshore-senegal-rises-26-2024-09-10/ (Reuters)]

'''International relations'''
*[[Belarus–European Union border crisis]], [[Germany–Poland relations]]
**[[Prime Minister of Poland]] [[Donald Tusk]] condemns [[Germany]]'s new [[Border|land border]] restrictions due to Germany's previous lack of support for other [[European Union]] nations impacted by [[irregular migration]]. [https://www.reuters.com/world/europe/polands-tusk-criticises-german-decision-tighten-border-controls-2024-09-10/ (Reuters)] [https://tvn24.pl/polska/niemcy-wprowadzaja-kontrole-na-wszystkich-granicach-ladowych-donald-tusk-komentuje-st8080239 (TVN24)]

'''Law and crime'''
*The [[Court of Justice of the European Union]] rules that [[Apple Inc.]] must pay €13 billion (US$14.3 billion) to the [[Government of Ireland|government]] of the [[Republic of Ireland]] as compensation for extraordinarily low taxes levied by Ireland against Apple. [https://www.euronews.com/my-europe/2024/09/10/apple-ireland-lose-13bn-sweetheart-tax-deal-case-in-victory-for-eus-tax-lady (Euronews)]
*[[Google]] is fined €2.4 billion (US$2.7 billion) by the [[Court of Justice of the European Union]] for favoring its own shopping search results over those of its competitors. [https://www.politico.eu/article/google-loses-court-battle-over-first-eu-antitrust-fine/ (Politico)]
*[[His Majesty's Prison Service]] begins releasing thousands of prisoners in [[England]] and [[Wales]] early amid a record high [[United Kingdom prison population|prison population]] and a shortage of prison cells for new inmates. [https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/live/c62rygz20gjt (BBC News)]
*A [[Switzerland|Swiss]] [[appeals court]] [[criminal conviction|convicts]] [[Ulama|Islamic scholar]] [[Tariq Ramadan]] of [[rape]] and [[sexual coercion]], [[sentence (law)|sentencing]] Ramadan to three years in prison, with two years suspension. [https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2024/9/10/swiss-court-convicts-islamic-scholar-on-rape-charges (Al Jazeera)] [https://www.bbc.com/news/articles/cx2n74n6q1vo (BBC News)]

'''Politics and elections'''
*[[2024 Jordanian general election]]
**[[Jordan]]ians go to the polls to elect all 138 members of the [[House of Representatives (Jordan)|House of Representatives]].  [https://www.npr.org/2024/09/10/g-s1-21747/jordanian-voters-go-to-polls-amid-fears-of-a-wider-war (NPR)]
*[[2024 Mexican judicial reform]]
**Protesters opposed to the ruling [[National Regeneration Movement|Morena]] party's reform package storm the [[Senate (Mexico)|Senate of Mexico]] and force an interruption of the bill's first reading in the upper house. The session reconvenes later at an alternative venue and passes the bill by an 86–41 vote. [https://www.theguardian.com/world/article/2024/sep/11/mexico-senate-approve-changes-judiciary (''The Guardian'')] [https://edition.cnn.com/2024/09/10/americas/mexico-judicial-reform-debate-senate-intl-latam/index.html (CNN)] 
*[[2021–present United Kingdom cost-of-living crisis]]
**The [[House of Commons of the United Kingdom]] votes 348–228 to end the [[Winter Fuel Payment]] for 10 million pensioners in England and [[Wales]] after [[Prime Minister of the United Kingdom|Prime Minister]] [[Keir Starmer]] warned that the scheme was no longer affordable to be applied universally. [https://news.sky.com/story/mps-vote-to-cut-winter-fuel-payment-for-millions-of-pensioners-13212264 (Sky News)]
*[[2024 United States presidential election]]
**A [[2024 United States presidential debates|presidential debate]] hosted by [[ABC News (United States)|ABC News]] between [[Vice President of the United States|U.S. vice president]] and [[2024 Democratic Party presidential candidates|Democratic nominee]] [[Kamala Harris]] and former president and [[2024 Republican Party presidential candidates|Republican nominee]] [[Donald Trump]] takes place at the [[National Constitution Center]] in [[Philadelphia]], [[Pennsylvania]]. [https://edition.cnn.com/politics/live-news/trump-harris-election-09-09-24/index.html (CNN)]
